audit_scope.description: Batch 13 includes EVM instruction implementations, SELFDESTRUCT semantics changes (EIP-6780), and protocol-level operations. Focus is on state-modifying operations and security-critical instruction behavior.

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction sender is the initiator of execution but not an external entity crossing the system boundary during execution. The transaction is already validated and internalized by the time SELFDESTRUCT is evaluated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Users via Transactions - SELFDESTRUCT Invocation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users can invoke smart contracts that execute SELFDESTRUCT opcode. Post-EIP-6780, SELFDESTRUCT only deletes contract if called in same transaction as creation, otherwise it just sends balance. Users might expect old SELFDESTRUCT behavior (immediate deletion) which could cause application logic errors. EL must enforce EIP-6780 restrictions.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: SELFDESTRUCT behavior changed in EIP-6780. Contract is only deleted if SELFDESTRUCT is called within the same transaction that created the contract. Otherwise, SELFDESTRUCT only transfers remaining balance to beneficiary address and marks contract for non-deletion. EL must track contract creation within transaction scope and enforce deletion restrictions. Beneficiary address receives balance regardless of deletion outcome.

coverage_gaps.reason: Batch 13 primarily covers internal EVM operations. External interaction is through transaction submission that triggers contract execution containing SELFDESTRUCT.
